reasons.reproducibility: Flasks are simple, but it uses PSP-toxic Alexandrium catenella, 300 L mesocosms and mussel saxitoxin assays.
reasons.effectiveness: -17-74% at 2-3 d and -42-96% at ~1 wk; kelp gave -73% in 48 h in mesocosms, though total chlorophyll did not fall.
reasons.cost: Mesocosms and saxitoxin analysis put it at $500-5,000.
reasons.environment: Seaweed is retrievable, but Ulva pushed pH to 9.0-9.5 (sometimes >10) and other algae replaced the target.

reasons.reproducibility: Needs ichthyotoxic Margalefidinium, larval fish in well plates and 300 L mesocosms.
reasons.effectiveness: -68%, -90% and -92% on days 5-7, but no reduction at all before day 5.
reasons.cost: Culture, fish and Ulva at 0.17-0.2 g/L are roughly $150-500 at bench scale.
reasons.environment: Live seaweed is retrievable and protected fish; no non-target harm reported.

reasons.reproducibility: 250 mL flasks with kelp/Ulva are simple, but Pseudo-nitzschia is a domoic-acid diatom bought from a culture centre.
reasons.effectiveness: -74-94% at >=72 h and -69 to -81% in bloom water with 2 g/L kelp, but Gracilaria and 1 g/L kelp had no significant effect.
reasons.cost: Culture plus seaweed and flasks is roughly $150-500.
reasons.environment: Seaweed is retrievable; only target diatoms were reported affected.

reasons.reproducibility: Fresh Ulva in flasks is easy, but the targets include toxic K. brevis and Karlodinium bought as cultures.
reasons.effectiveness: Only -24% to -50% at 72 h across species, though extracts lysed two species after 5 d.
reasons.cost: Several cultures plus seaweed are roughly $150-500.
reasons.environment: Seaweed is retrievable; allelochemicals are heat-stable but no non-target harm reported.

reasons.reproducibility: Axenic Heterosigma and Alexandrium cultures co-cultured with collected Ulva need a sponsor.
reasons.effectiveness: Ulva killed all H. akashiwo at 5-10 g-wet/L (n=3) but never killed A. tamarense, filtrate had no effect and low powder doses stimulated growth.
reasons.cost: Two cultures, f/2 medium and Ulva cost about $150-500.
reasons.time: H. akashiwo died within 2 days (lysis LT50 3-7 h).
reasons.environment: Living Ulva is retrievable, though grams per litre of seaweed are needed.

reasons.reproducibility: Eight axenic microalgal cultures with fresh Ulva in flasks is sponsor-level work.
reasons.effectiveness: Ulva killed H. akashiwo and Skeletonema 100% and cut others 21-90% in triplicate, including nutrient-replete tests that rule out competition.
reasons.cost: Eight cultures and media cost $150-500.
reasons.environment: Living Ulva is removable; nutrients stayed replete.

reasons.reproducibility: Collected Ulva and one P. micans culture in f/2 flasks are simple bench work.
reasons.effectiveness: Ulva tissue and powder cut growth dose-dependently in 4 replicates and 10 g/L fresh or 2.4 g/L powder killed the cultures.
reasons.cost: One culture plus free seaweed costs about $50-150.
reasons.time: Powder at 2.4 g/L killed cultures within 4 days.
reasons.environment: Seaweed is natural and removable, though powder adds organic matter at high doses.

reasons.reproducibility: Four dinoflagellate cultures (including toxic Alexandrium) with collected seaweed need a sponsor.
reasons.effectiveness: Ulva killed three of four dinoflagellates within 144 h in triplicate; Gracilaria mostly acted through nutrient depletion.
reasons.cost: Four cultures and media cost $150-500.
reasons.time: LT50s were 38-64 h and all cells were dead within 6 days.
reasons.environment: Living thalli are retrievable; filtrates stimulated some species.

reasons.reproducibility: Ulva co-culture with purchased HAB cultures including toxic A. tamarense.
reasons.effectiveness: -48% A. tamarense at 0.8 g/L; filtrate worked only for 2 d before recovery.
reasons.cost: Cultures plus seaweed are roughly $150-500.
reasons.environment: Not reported; live seaweed is retrievable.

reasons.reproducibility: 4-hour assays in 24-well plates with dried Ulva powder and a Heterosigma culture are simple bench work.
reasons.effectiveness: Powder LC50 0.40-0.70 g/L DW, but fresh tissue at 50 g/L killed only 1.6-6.6% in 4 h.
reasons.cost: One culture, well plates and seaweed are about $50-150.
reasons.environment: Dried powder cannot be retrieved, though its PUFAs fell to 2% of peak by 48 h (short-lived).

reasons.reproducibility: One Heterosigma culture with fresh Ulva or Gracilaria is straightforward bench work.
reasons.effectiveness: Ulva >=0.68 g FW/L killed all H. akashiwo in triplicate, but 0.34 g/L cut only ~53% and low Gracilaria or extract doses stimulated growth 56-72%.
reasons.cost: One culture plus collected seaweed costs about $50-150.
reasons.time: LT50s were 36-83 h and all cells died within 5 days.
reasons.environment: Living seaweed is removable; Gracilaria depleted nutrients.

reasons.reproducibility: Seven HAB cultures, brown-tide field water and a larval fish bioassay need a sponsor.
reasons.effectiveness: Lab thalli cut A. anophagefferens >97% but other species only 20-64%, and in natural brown-tide water only 13-44%.
reasons.cost: Several HAB cultures and fish cost $150-500.
reasons.time: Lab tests ran 5 days and field bottles 48 h.
reasons.environment: No sheepshead minnow mortality at 900 mg dry wt/L and inhibition was not nutrient competition.

reasons.reproducibility: Lab and bottle tests are doable, but the study also used 50 L and 1000 L mesocosms with kilograms of farmed Gracilaria.
reasons.effectiveness: Bloom-water bottles fell 75-88% and 50 L mesocosms 70-82% vs controls in triplicate, though the 1000 L treatment overtook the control after day 8.
reasons.cost: Mesocosms and kilograms of seaweed cost $500-5,000.
reasons.time: Bottle reductions reached 75-88% by day 3, mesocosms by day 8.
reasons.environment: Living seaweed is harvestable and species richness was higher with Gracilaria.

reasons.reproducibility: Simple 500 mL co-culture, but Ostreopsis makes palytoxin-like toxins and pH must be held at 8.
reasons.effectiveness: Ulva co-culture ended 94% below the inoculum, but powder gave only -17-37% and filtrate stimulated growth.
reasons.cost: Culture, seaweeds and pH control are roughly $150-500.
reasons.time: LT50 of 12 d over a 20-day run.
reasons.environment: Seaweed is retrievable; Ulva drew down DIN and target cells formed cysts.

reasons.reproducibility: 200 mL co-cultures are simple, but targets include toxic Ostreopsis, P. lima and A. pacificum.
reasons.effectiveness: Growth rates fell 35-62% in benthic species and A. pacificum all died by day 6 at >=0.8 g/L.
reasons.cost: Four cultures plus seaweed are roughly $150-500.
reasons.time: A. pacificum was all dead by day 6.
reasons.environment: pH, DO and nutrients did not differ from controls; seaweed is retrievable.

reasons.reproducibility: 250 mL flasks with local Gracilaria and an Aureococcus culture (no human toxin) are school-feasible.
reasons.effectiveness: Lab reductions needed >=0.75-1 g/L and >=72 h; in field bottles only Dasysiphonia at 3 g/L gave -30% and Gracilaria was not significant.
reasons.cost: One culture plus seaweed is about $50-150.
reasons.environment: pH 9.0 alone inhibited Aureococcus, so part of the effect is a pH side-effect, and Dasysiphonia is invasive.

reasons.reproducibility: The co-culture is simple, but the mechanism work used metabolomics and PSII analysis.
reasons.effectiveness: Fresh thalli inhibited the fouling diatom dose-dependently (IC50 0.667 g/L at day 4, n=3), but the lowest extract dose was ineffective and the target is not a HAB.
reasons.cost: Culture and seaweed are cheap; PSII and metabolomic work bring it to $150-500.
reasons.environment: Living seaweed is removable, though it releases taurine and isethionic acid.

reasons.reproducibility: The lab part is simple, but the headline trial uses kelp lines on an oyster farm.
reasons.effectiveness: Measures pH (7.44 to 8.42 at 1 g/L), not any reduction of HAB cells.
reasons.cost: Kelp lines and farm monitoring are $500-5,000.
reasons.environment: Kelp raised pH (+0.15 in field), a co-benefit against acidification, and is harvested.

reasons.reproducibility: Kelp longline farming at three Long Island Sound sites needs boats and permits.
reasons.effectiveness: No phytoplankton or HAB outcome was measured; only nutrient extraction.
reasons.cost: Longline farms cost over $5,000.
reasons.environment: Kelp removes nitrogen and carbon, with no added material.

reasons.reproducibility: The typical reviewed experiment is a simple seaweed-microalga co-culture in flasks.
reasons.effectiveness: Lists confounders (nutrients, shading, pH, bacteria) and notes few studies held pH constant, so reported effects are hard to trust.
reasons.cost: A typical co-culture study is about $50-150.
reasons.time: Typical reviewed co-cultures last several days to ~2 weeks.
reasons.environment: Seaweed is retrievable, but Ulva can push pH above 10.
